summary: Additive public-API change to @cipherstash/stack (changeset: minor). It re-exports ten operation classes from the ./encryption entry and four from the ./dynamodb entry, removes @internal tags from EncryptQueryOperation/BatchEncryptQueryOperation and their WithLockContext variants, adds EncryptedQuery and EncryptedFromSchema to ./types, and fixes TSDoc (type-only imports used only for {@link}). No encryption, decryption, lock-context or payload logic changes; the re-exports are bindings already imported by those modules, so no new module-graph edges are introduced. The material consequence is contractual: class constructors (which take internal types such as the FFI Client) become part of the semver-covered public surface, and different classes named EncryptModelOperation, BulkEncryptModelsOperation etc. are now exported from two subpaths. Impact is low; normal review is sufficient. Nothing was built or run.

behaviour_changes.description: @cipherstash/stack/encryption now exports (as runtime values) EncryptOperation, EncryptQueryOperation, BatchEncryptQueryOperation, DecryptOperation, EncryptModelOperation, DecryptModelOperation, BulkEncryptOperation, BulkDecryptOperation, BulkEncryptModelsOperation, BulkDecryptModelsOperation, including their public constructors.

@cipherstash/stack/dynamodb now exports its own EncryptModelOperation, DecryptModelOperation, BulkEncryptModelsOperation and BulkDecryptModelsOperation classes (distinct classes from the same-named encryption ones; constructors take an EncryptionClient).
@cipherstash/stack/types adds type exports EncryptedQuery and EncryptedFromSchema (type-only; erased at runtime).

@internal TSDoc tags removed from EncryptQueryOperation, BatchEncryptQueryOperation and their WithLockContext variants (the WithLockContext classes are still not re-exported from an entry point); TSDoc fixes and type-only imports added for {@link} resolution; a @param name corrected in buildEncryptConfig docs.
A changeset bumps @cipherstash/stack by a minor version and asserts no runtime behaviour change.

failure_scenarios.title: Operation class constructors become a semver-locked public contract
failure_scenarios.trigger: A later release refactors an operation constructor (e.g. EncryptOperation(client, plaintext, opts) or the DynamoDB EncryptModelOperation(encryptionClient, item, table, options)) in a minor/patch version after consumers start instantiating or subclassing the now-exported classes.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The classes are exported as values, not `export type`, so their constructors (which take internal shapes such as the FFI `Client` type) are now reachable public API. Previously only the instances returned by EncryptionClient/encryptedDynamoDB methods were public. The changeset frames the change as type-naming only.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Consumer code that constructs or extends these classes breaks at compile time or runtime after an otherwise routine internal refactor; maintainers lose freedom to change constructor signatures without a major bump. No data or security consequence: constructing an operation directly still needs a client, and the wrapped FFI calls are unchanged.
missing_verification: No test or API-surface snapshot asserts which names each entry point exports or whether constructors are intended to be public.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Either export the classes with `export type { ... }` (sufficient for naming return types and TSDoc links), or mark constructors @internal / document that only the returned instances are supported.

failure_scenarios.title: Same class names exported from two subpaths refer to different classes
failure_scenarios.trigger: A consumer names the return type of encryptedDynamoDB(...).encryptModel() using EncryptModelOperation imported from @cipherstash/stack/encryption (or vice versa), e.g. via IDE auto-import.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: encryption/index.ts and dynamodb/index.ts both export EncryptModelOperation, DecryptModelOperation, BulkEncryptModelsOperation and BulkDecryptModelsOperation, but they are different classes with different constructors and result/error types.
failure_scenarios.consequence: TypeScript type errors or confusing type mismatches in consumer code; loud at compile time, no runtime data effect.
missing_verification: No type test covers naming the DynamoDB operation types.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Document the distinction in TSDoc, or alias the DynamoDB exports (e.g. DynamoDBEncryptModelOperation).
